CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

**(1) Server instructions from freecad-buddy-docker, verbatim:**

> FreeCAD Buddy drives a live FreeCAD document through typed tools. Tool families:
> - document_: create, open, save, close, list, recompute and undo documents.
> - query_: read-only facts: tree, objects, sketches, placement, dependencies, mass properties, screenshots, capabilities.
> - verify_: check shapes, sketches and recomputes against numbers.
> - export_ and verify_export_: write STEP, STL or 3MF, then check the written file.
> - sketch_: create sketches; add, remove and constrain geometry.
> - feature_: PartDesign bodies and features (pad, pocket, revolve, hole, fillet, chamfer, pattern, mirror, datum) and their parameters.
> - preview_: dry-run a mutation before it is applied.
> - view_: fit the 3D viewport.
>
> Use a typed tool whenever one covers the operation. Before a build, make the sketch_, feature_, query_ and verify_ tools available in your client.
>
> script_exec is for the gaps listed in the freecad-scripting-idioms skill.
>
> Load these skills first: design-decomposition, freecad-sketcher, freecad-partdesign, verification-thinking.

**(2) Tool load state:**

- Loaded with full schema: none of the freecad-buddy-docker tools.
- Deferred, with only names known, so calls fail until I load the schemas:
  - document_: close, create, list, open, recompute, save, undo
  - export_: 3mf, step, stl
  - feature_: body_create, chamfer, datum, fillet, hole, mirror, pad, pattern, pocket, revolve, set_parameters
  - preview_dry_run
  - query_: capabilities, dependencies, mass_properties, object, placement, screenshot, sketch_info, tree_summary
  - script_exec
  - sketch_: add_constraint, add_external_geometry, add_geometry, create, remove_constraint, remove_geometry, set_datum, toggle_construction
  - verify_: export_3mf, export_step, export_stl, recompute, shape, sketch
  - view_fit_viewport

Next I load the schemas for the tools I need and the four skills the server names.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\thuan\.claude\plugins\cache\freecad-buddy\freecad-buddy\0.1.1\design-decomposition

## Scope

Turn a request into an ordered build plan a copilot can execute one feature at a
time. This skill owns the *plan*: what the base solid is, which plane it sketches
on, the order features attach in, and whether the result is one body or several.
It does not own sketch constraint strategy (sketch-strategy) or picking a single
operation like pad-vs-revolve (tool-selection) — it decides the sequence those
operations run in. It also owns the one-question clarification gate and the
extraction of a drawing or image into a modeling brief. Assembly *strategy*
(mating surfaces, degrees of freedom) is out of scope for now; here you only
decide part-vs-assembly and hand a body list downstream.

The plan you produce is executed through the **freecad-buddy MCP server** (the
`query_*`, `verify_*`, and `sketch_*`/`feature_*` tools the plan hands to). If those
tools aren't available in your session, install and connect the freecad-buddy MCP
first — open FreeCAD with the freecad-buddy add-on, which auto-starts the server,
then point your MCP client at it — otherwise the plan can't be built.

## Decision Rules

- Pick the construction that makes the spec's controlling dimensions **direct
  parameters**, because a dimension the user stated should be a driving value, not
  something derived. Profile-driven shapes → one closed sketch plus a single
  pad/revolve/sweep/loft; block-and-feature parts → a base solid plus subtractive
  features.
- Choose the base solid and its sketch plane from the **functional datum** —
  the mounting face, mating interface, or symmetry axis — before planning
  features, because the frame you model in is the frame every later reference and
  measurement lives in.
- Order features so fragile steps land last and a failure points at one feature:
  **base solid → major additions → subtractive features → shell → through-wall
  holes → fillets and chamfers last.** Fillets are the most failure-prone step and
  every prior boolean re-labels the edges a fillet selects, so postponing them
  keeps selectors valid and localizes blame (fillet failure modes: see
  freecad-partdesign).
- Make each planned feature a **named step** with an intent-bearing name, because
  the feature tree should read like the build plan and a parameter edit should
  touch one obvious place.
- Write the plan in the **CAD plan shape**: a parameter table (name, value, unit,
  source — spec, callout, or assumption) and a list of milestones, each a finished
  part or feature group with the spec checks that close it. No per-step checkboxes
  and no hand-predicted volumes: each mutation result already reports what changed
  and what failed, and a volume worked out by hand is a second, unchecked model.
- Close each milestone only after its `verify_shape` checks and screenshot pass:
  then `document_save`, then, when the user's project uses version control, one
  commit of the `.FCStd` and the plan file — one commit per milestone, so every
  commit is a verified state to return to.
- Keep **derived pieces** — print splits, `Part::Common` cuts of a master body —
  out of the edit loop: put them in a separate document, or rebuild them only at
  milestones, because every master-body change recomputes each one. On
  `kiwibox-drawer.FCStd`, 3 split `Part::Common` objects took 7.5 s of the 14.6 s
  recompute after one change to the master body. No typed tool creates a
  `Part::Common`, so make or rebuild them through the closed-document script
  fallback in freecad-scripting-idioms.
- Decide single body vs multiple bodies before modeling: parts that are
  separately manufactured, purchased, or movable are separate bodies; one
  monolithic manufacturing intent is one fused solid. Never emit an unlabeled
  multi-body result — traceability in `query_tree_summary` depends on names.
- Plan references defensively: a later feature that attaches to a face or edge
  should target a **datum plane or a geometric-query/mapped-name selector**, not a
  bare `Face6`, because indices reshuffle on recompute (TNP). Prefer creating a
  datum early over referencing a face that a later boolean will invalidate.
- When a technical drawing drives the model, read the title block (units,
  projection) and map each view to a model axis **before** extracting numbers, then
  convert every callout into a named parameter and a validation target — because a
  drawing is a dimensioned contract, and every callout must end up checkable by
  `verify_shape`/`query_mass_properties` or explicitly reported as unverified.
- A reference image without stated dimensions is **design intent, not a spec**:
  establish scale from one stated dimension or a known object, estimate the rest,
  and record every estimate as an assumption.
- When sources conflict, dimensioned beats proportion, and two conflicting
  dimensioned sources get **flagged, not silently resolved** — a silent choice
  hides an error the user could have caught.
- Ask exactly **one** clarification only when the answer changes the geometry and
  can't be assumed: no dimensions and no scale reference, a mating interface named
  but unspecified, a safety/load/pressure/compliance-critical part, or a missing
  source file. Otherwise proceed with stated assumptions — asking for a defaultable
  clearance hole, a cosmetic fillet radius, or a choosable origin wastes a turn.

## Worked Examples

Input: "Design a mounting bracket: 60×40×5 mm base plate, two M5 through-holes
40 mm apart, one perpendicular flange 30 mm tall with a 10 mm lightening slot."

Reasoning → plan:
1. Base solid = the 60×40×5 plate; sketch on XY, functional datum = the mounting
   face (plate underside), origin at plate center so the hole pattern is symmetric.
   Controlling params: `plate_len=60`, `plate_wid=40`, `plate_thk=5`,
   `hole_spacing=40`, `hole_dia=5.5` (M5 clearance).
2. Two through-holes next (subtractive), positioned from `hole_spacing` about the
   center — not from a plate edge, so they stay symmetric under a length edit.
3. Flange = a second pad on a datum plane at the plate end (create the datum
   early; don't reference the plate's end face, which the holes' recompute could
   re-label). `flange_ht=30`.
4. Lightening slot = subtractive pocket on the flange. `slot_len=10`.
5. No fillets requested → none planned. One body (monolithic bracket).
No clarification needed: M5 clearance is defaultable, origin is choosable-and-
reported. Milestones: M1 plate with holes (bbox 60×40×5, 2 holes Ø5.5 at 40 mm
spacing); M2 flange and slot (bbox ≈ 60×40×35, flange perpendicular, one valid
solid). Once its checks pass, each closes with `document_save` and, under version
control, one commit.

Input: a 2D drawing, front view labelled "Ø12 THRU, 4X", title block "mm, third-
angle".

Reasoning: units = mm (from title block, not assumed); "4X Ø12 THRU" → one pocket
feature patterned 4× → parameters `hole_dia=12`, `hole_count=4` → validation
targets `count_cylindrical_holes == 4`, `hole_diameter == 12`. Map the front view
to the XY face before reading positions. Any position dimension missing from the
drawing is reported as unverified, never scaled off the image.

## Anti-Patterns

- **Planning fillets early.** Symptom: a later boolean fails or its edge selector
  breaks. Why: booleans re-label edges, invalidating the fillet's selection. Fix:
  fillets/chamfers are the last planned step.
- **Modeling before choosing the origin.** Symptom: alignment and hole-symmetry
  checks are ambiguous downstream. Why: an arbitrary origin means every relative
  measurement has an arbitrary reference. Fix: fix the functional datum first.
- **Deriving a stated dimension.** Symptom: the user edits "plate length" and the
  hole spacing doesn't follow, or vice versa. Why: the controlling dimension became
  a computed value instead of a parameter. Fix: choose the construction that makes
  stated dimensions direct parameters.
- **Referencing a face a later step invalidates.** Symptom: `post_verify.tnp_audit`
  reports `BROKEN`/`REPOINTED` findings after recompute. Why: a bare face index moved when the
  tree recomputed (TNP). Fix: attach to a datum plane or a geometric-query selector.
- **A per-step checklist plan.** Symptom: a checkbox and a predicted volume for
  every feature, and a check call after each one. Why: the plan repeats what each
  mutation result reports, and the hand math drifts from the model. Fix: a
  parameter table and milestones; verify per milestone.
- **Unlabeled multi-body output.** Symptom: `query_tree_summary` lists
  `[BODY] Body`, `[BODY] Body001`; inspection can't tell which is which. Why:
  bodies with no intent names lose traceability. Fix: name every body from its role.
- **Asking a question you could assume.** Symptom: a turn spent asking for a
  clearance-hole size or a cosmetic fillet. Why: the answer was defaultable and
  reportable. Fix: proceed with a stated assumption; reserve the one question for
  fit/safety/missing-source cases.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\thuan\.claude\plugins\cache\freecad-buddy\freecad-buddy\0.1.1\freecad-sketcher

## Scope

Drive a single sketch to a clean, fully constrained state and know how its
constraint solver behaves. This skill owns the sketch interior: geometry vs
construction geometry, the constraint types and what each removes, reaching
DoF = 0, and the special risk of external-geometry references. It does not own the
feature a sketch feeds (freecad-partdesign) or the decision of how many sketches a
part needs (sketch-strategy) — it owns one sketch once you're in it.

This skill drives FreeCAD through the **freecad-buddy MCP server** (the `query_*`,
`verify_*`, and `sketch_*` tools named below). If those tools aren't available in
your session, install and connect the freecad-buddy MCP first — open FreeCAD with
the freecad-buddy add-on, which auto-starts the server, then point your MCP client
at it — otherwise none of these steps can run.

## Decision Rules

- Treat a sketch as done only when the last `sketch_*` result reports
  `structured_content.sketch_state.fully_constrained` true and `dof` 0, with
  `mutation.post_verify.passed` true. That is the AD-8 sketch signal: the same
  grade `verify_sketch` computes (a clean solve, no conflicting, malformed or
  redundant constraint), so do not call `verify_sketch` after a typed sketch
  tool. `sketch_state.readable` false (no grade) or a `"not_measured"`
  `fully_constrained` is not a pass: call `verify_sketch`. Call `verify_sketch`
  also for a sketch changed outside the typed tools (a GUI edit, a script),
  because no mutation result covers that change. FreeCAD's
  `FullyConstrained` property alone is not enough, because FreeCAD does not update
  it after a failed solve, so a redundant sketch can keep a stale true.
- Never infer degrees of freedom from a successful solve: `solve()` returning 0
  means "solved", not "fully constrained", because the solver happily converges on
  an under-constrained sketch by holding the free parameters where they sit.
- Constrain **construction geometry first**, then hang real geometry off it,
  because construction lines and points carry the design skeleton (centerlines,
  bolt-circle radii) and constraining them first makes the rest fall into place
  with fewer, clearer constraints.
- Prefer **symmetric and equal constraints over duplicated dimensions**, because
  one symmetry constraint captures the intent ("these are mirrored") in a way a
  later edit preserves, whereas two equal numbers silently drift apart when one is
  changed.
- Add constraints in the order geometric → dimensional: lock the shape
  (coincident, horizontal, vertical, parallel, perpendicular, tangent, equal,
  symmetric) before the sizes (distance, radius, angle), because dimensioning
  un-located geometry produces a solver fighting to place and size at once, which is
  where conflicts appear.
- Treat **conflicting**, **malformed** and **redundant** constraints as a hard
  failure, because FreeCAD marks a redundant sketch in error and builds no shape for
  it. Only **partially redundant** constraints are a warning. Remove the redundant
  constraint the diagnostic names; never add a constraint "to be safe".
- Map a solver constraint id back to its constraint by name when reporting a
  conflict — the solver reports 1-based ids, and naming the actual constraint is
  what makes the diagnosis actionable.
- Use **external geometry with caution**: projecting a model edge or face into a
  sketch creates a reference that a later recompute can re-point or drop (the
  topological-naming risk), so prefer attaching to a datum plane over projecting a
  face, and after any change read the reference audit in
  `mutation.post_verify.tnp_audit` — an `UNSUPPORTED` status or finding is not
  clean.
- Keep degenerate geometry out: a zero-length edge or a coincident-endpoints line
  passes a casual glance but fails the solve or the downstream feature. Fix it in
  the sketch, not by working around it downstream.

## Worked Examples

Input: "Constrain this rectangle sketch to 60×40 centered on the origin."

Reasoning → constraints:
1. Geometry constraints first: the four lines get horizontal/vertical, endpoints
   coincident to close the loop.
2. Symmetry: constrain the rectangle symmetric about the origin in X and in Y —
   one symmetric constraint per axis, not four corner dimensions — so a later width
   edit stays centered.
3. Dimensions: one horizontal distance = 60, one vertical distance = 40.
4. Send the lines and all these constraints in one `sketch_add_geometry` call —
   geometry sent alone leaves `dof` > 0, which fails and rolls back. Its result →
   `sketch_state.fully_constrained` true, `dof` 0, `post_verify.passed` true, no
   conflicting or redundant constraints. Done — no separate `verify_sketch` call.
If instead you'd dimensioned all four corners from the origin, the sketch would be
over-defined the moment you added the width, and the solver would report a conflict.

Input: "I added two holes to the sketch in the GUI; is it still fine?"

Reasoning: the edit was made outside the typed tools, so no mutation result covers
it — call `verify_sketch`. It reports `dof` 2: the two hole centers are unlocated.
Add the missing position constraints in one `sketch_add_constraint` call — distances
from a construction centerline, or a symmetry constraint if the holes are mirrored.
Its `sketch_state` reports `fully_constrained` true and `dof` 0. Never pad the
feature before that.

## Anti-Patterns

- **Reading DoF from the solver code.** Symptom: an under-constrained sketch
  treated as done. Why: `solve() == 0` means "solved", not "fully constrained". Fix:
  gate on `sketch_state.fully_constrained` and `dof`.
- **Duplicated dimensions instead of symmetry.** Symptom: an edit makes a
  once-symmetric feature lopsided. Why: two equal numbers drift when one changes.
  Fix: use a symmetric or equal constraint.
- **Dimensioning before locating.** Symptom: the solver reports conflicts as you
  add sizes. Why: shape and size were fought at once. Fix: geometric constraints
  first, dimensions second.
- **Keeping a redundant constraint.** Symptom: the mutation rolls back with
  `RECOMPUTE_ERROR` "Sketch with redundant constraints". Why: FreeCAD fails a
  redundant sketch. Fix: remove the constraint the diagnostic names.
- **Projecting a face for an external reference.** Symptom: the sketch breaks after
  an unrelated recompute. Why: the projected edge was re-pointed or dropped (TNP).
  Fix: attach to a datum plane where possible; read `post_verify.tnp_audit` after
  each change.

## Scope

Drive individual PartDesign features correctly and know how each one fails. This
skill owns per-feature knowledge: what a pad/pocket/revolution/hole/fillet/chamfer/
loft/sweep/pattern/mirror needs before it will run, the properties that control it,
and the trap each one falls into. It does not own the *order* features run in
(design-decomposition) or the sketches they consume (freecad-sketcher) — it owns
the operation once its input exists. The full per-feature prerequisite and
failure-mode tables live in `references/feature-failure-tables.md`; load that when
a specific feature misbehaves.

This skill drives FreeCAD through the **freecad-buddy MCP server** (the `feature_*`,
`query_*`, and `verify_*` tools named below). If those tools aren't available in your
session, install and connect the freecad-buddy MCP first — open FreeCAD with the
freecad-buddy add-on, which auto-starts the server, then point your MCP client at
it — otherwise none of these steps can run.

## Decision Rules

- Give a solid-adding or -removing feature a valid **closed profile** before
  running it, because pad and pocket are profile-based — an open wire produces no
  face and the feature fails or yields a null shape.
- Set a pad/pocket's length mode deliberately: `Type = "Length"` for a fixed
  extent, or an up-to mode (`"UpToFace"`, `"UpToShape"`, and for pad `"UpToLast"`/
  `"UpToFirst"`, for pocket `"ThroughAll"`) when the extent should follow existing
  geometry — the enum members differ between pad and pocket, so confirm the exact
  value with `query_object` rather than assuming. Use `Midplane` to grow symmetric
  about the sketch and
  `Reversed` to flip direction rather than negating the length.
- **Overshoot a through-cut**: extend the cutting profile roughly 1 mm past the
  faces it enters and exits (or use a through-all/up-to mode), because a tool face
  coincident or coplanar with a target face is a classic OCCT boolean failure.
- **Cut a repeated feature once, then pattern it** — model one hole/pocket and
  apply a linear or polar pattern (`Occurrences` controls the count) rather than
  placing N separate features, because one patterned feature is one named step that
  edits and verifies as a unit.
- Apply **fillets and chamfers last**, because every boolean before them re-labels
  the edges they select; a fillet added early loses its edge references when a
  later feature recomputes. Fillet's control is `Radius`; chamfer's is `Size` (with
  `ChamferType` and `Angle` for the equal/two-distance/distance-angle variants).
- Keep a fillet `Radius` (or chamfer `Size`) **smaller than the local geometry** it
  rounds, because a radius larger than the adjacent face or edge length has no valid
  solution and the dress-up fails.
- Select the edges/faces a feature references by **datum, axis, position, or a
  geometric-query/mapped-name selector**, never a bare `Face6`/`Edge3`, because
  indices reshuffle on recompute (TNP) and a fillet's edge list silently drops
  members that lose their two adjacent faces.
- Give a loft/sweep ordered, compatible profiles: a loft needs its `Sections` in
  sequence (set `Closed` to loop the last back to the first, `Ruled` for straight
  transitions); a sweep needs a `Spine` path plus its section(s), and a self-
  intersecting or sharply-kinked spine is the usual sweep failure.
- Give a hole feature a sketch of its center points, then set `Diameter`,
  `DepthType`, and (if tapped) `Threaded` — the thread and counterbore/countersink
  metadata (`HoleCutType`, `ThreadDiameter`) is descriptive, so verify the actual
  cut geometry, not the property values.
- After any feature, treat a clean recompute as necessary but not sufficient:
  measure the result against intent and audit references — recompute success only
  proves the script ran (verification is owned by verification-thinking).

## Worked Examples

Input: "Pad this rectangular sketch 5 mm, then put four Ø5.5 holes and round the
top edges 2 mm."

Reasoning → operations:
1. Pad the closed rectangle: `Type = "Length"`, `Length = 5`. Verify one valid
   solid, bbox thickness 5 mm.
2. Holes: one hole-point sketch with the four centers, one Hole feature
   `Diameter = 5.5` `DepthType` through — patterned from the sketch, not four
   features. Overshoot is automatic for a through hole.
3. Fillet **last**: select the four top edges by "top face + its bounding edges"
   (position/axis), not by index; `Radius = 2`. Because the holes were cut before
   the fillet, the fillet's edge references are stable.
If the fillet had been added before the holes, the holes' recompute would have
re-labelled the top edges and the fillet would report dropped edges.

Input: "The 4 mm fillet on this 3 mm-thick web fails."

Reasoning: `Radius = 4` exceeds the local 3 mm geometry — no valid rounding fits.
Fix per `references/feature-failure-tables.md`: reduce the radius below the local
thickness, or narrow the edge selection, or split the edge group by intent.

## Anti-Patterns

- **Fillet-before-boolean.** Symptom: dropped-edge or recompute error after a later
  feature. Why: the boolean re-labelled the filleted edges. Fix: fillets/chamfers
  are the last features.
- **Coincident cut faces.** Symptom: a through-pocket leaves a thin skin or the
  boolean errors. Why: the tool face sits exactly on the target face. Fix: overshoot
  ~1 mm or use a through-all/up-to mode.
- **N separate features for a pattern.** Symptom: an edit means changing N features
  and they drift. Why: the repetition wasn't captured as one feature. Fix: model one
  and pattern it with `Occurrences`.
- **Index-based edge selection.** Symptom: a fillet or chamfer references the wrong
  edge after recompute, or silently drops one. Why: `Edge3` moved (TNP), and dress-up
  drops edges that lose adjacency. Fix: select by datum/axis/position or a
  geometric-query selector.
- **Radius larger than local geometry.** Symptom: fillet/chamfer fails with no
  clear message. Why: no valid solution fits the adjacent faces. Fix: shrink the
  radius/size below the local dimension.
- **Open profile into a pad/pocket.** Symptom: null shape or feature error. Why:
  a profile-based feature needs a closed face. Fix: close the sketch profile first
  (freecad-sketcher).

## Scope

Decide what "done" means for a modeled part and prove it. This skill owns the
verification mindset: which deterministic checks a spec demands, why a clean
recompute is necessary but never sufficient, when a render is mandatory, and how
to convert a visual concern into a measurement before it counts as a result. It
covers per-part done-ness, not per-operation transaction safety (the mutation
protocol handles rollback automatically) and not error diagnosis
(freecad-troubleshooting). Snapshot packet sizing lives in
`references/snapshot-packet-sizing.md`, loaded when a review needs more than one
view.

Every check here runs through the **freecad-buddy MCP server** (the `query_*` and
`verify_*` tools named below). If those tools aren't available in your session,
install and connect the freecad-buddy MCP first — open FreeCAD with the
freecad-buddy add-on, which auto-starts the server, then point your MCP client at
it — otherwise none of these checks can run.

## Decision Rules

- Treat the producing agent's own judgement as **input, never a verdict** — pass
  or fail comes from deterministic checks (`verify_shape`, `verify_sketch`,
  `verify_export_step`) or an independent judge, because an agent that grades its
  own work systematically over-scores it.
- Verify on the **build loop**, not on every call. **Per feature:** read the
  mutation result — `structured_content.mutation.post_verify`,
  `structured_content.sketch_state` on a sketch tool, and `mutation.changed` —
  with no `verify_*` call and no screenshot, because every mutation already ran
  those checks. Clean = `passed` true, `tnp_audit.status` `CLEAN`, no
  `"not_measured"` field (detail: `references/reading-mutation-results.md`).
  **Per milestone** (a finished part or feature group): one `verify_shape` whose
  `checks` carry every spec check, and one screenshot packet. **After a change outside the typed tools** (a GUI edit, a
  script, the user): run `verify_recompute`, `verify_shape`, and `verify_sketch`.
  No tool audits references or compares before and after outside a mutation, so
  report reference integrity and freedom from regression as unverified.
- On a **failed mutation** (`post_verify.passed` false): with `rolled_back` true
  and `rollback_proven` set, the change is not in the model — read `explanation`,
  fix the cause, send the call again. With `rolled_back` false or
  `rollback_proven` null, the model state is unproven: stop and report.
- A clean recompute is **necessary but not sufficient**: `verify_recompute`
  passing means the script ran, not that the geometry is right. Always follow it
  with spec-driven measurement, because "a pocket exists" is not "the right pocket,
  right place, right depth".
- Measure **every** dimension, offset, and clearance the spec (or a drawing
  callout) states — with `query_mass_properties` for bbox/volume and
  `query_placement` for distances and offsets — because an unchecked dimension is
  an unverified claim, and the point of verifying is to falsify a wrong part.
- Run a baseline inspection at each milestone before the spec checks:
  `query_tree_summary` (`focus` on the body) for names and `!<status>` errors,
  `query_mass_properties` for a scale sanity check. An order-of-magnitude or
  centering error passes narrow checks but shows up in the baseline.
- Check an interface that should be flush or centered with `query_placement`
  deltas between the two references; if it's off, fix the source feature or datum
  and recompute — never nudge exported geometry, because the model is the source
  of truth and the export is derived.
- On a **modification**, compare `mutation.fingerprint_before.digest` with
  `fingerprint_after.digest` (equal means no geometry changed) and read
  `mutation.changed`, the objects whose mass properties differ, because a change
  that "worked" may have silently altered an unrelated feature. In a PartDesign
  body each feature's `Shape` is cumulative, so an edit also lists every later
  feature and the body; an *earlier* feature in `changed` is the regression. A
  null `fingerprint_*` leaves `changed` empty: the regression check is unverified,
  so re-measure. Never use file size or a diff of the saved document as a
  geometry comparison — those change for reasons unrelated to shape.
- An export counts as done **only** when its paired `verify_export_step` (or
  `_stl`/`_3mf`) re-imports and matches, because "the file was written" is not
  proof the geometry survived the round-trip. Independent-oracle disagreement is a
  fail, never an average.
- After any mutation, read `post_verify.tnp_audit.status` (the post-recompute
  reference audit): `CLEAN`; `FLAGGED` (a `BROKEN`, `REPOINTED`, `DROPPED`, or
  `UNSUPPORTED` finding); or `UNSUPPORTED` (the audit could not run).
  `RE_BASELINED` is informational and can appear under `CLEAN`. `UNSUPPORTED` is
  *not clean*, yet `passed` stays true on it, so read the status separately — a
  silently re-pointed reference is a corrupted model that still recomputes.
- Take a screenshot with `query_screenshot` for every milestone, **even when
  every deterministic check passed**, because deterministic
  checks only catch what the spec encoded; a mirrored part or a feature on the
  wrong face passes the numbers and fails the eye. Size the packet per
  `references/snapshot-packet-sizing.md`; don't re-render in a loop.
- **Convert every visual concern into a geometry check before it becomes a
  result** — a screenshot is diagnostic, not authoritative. "Holes look
  asymmetric" → measure the hole centers; "the lid looks offset" → check the frame
  delta; "a boss looks floating" → check the solid count and contact. The
  measurement is the claim; the render only pointed at it.
- A generated *part* is done only when **both** channels pass: all geometry
  assertions AND an independent visual judge (a vision model that is never the
  acting agent). The judge is conjunctive — it can flag a wrong-looking part that
  geometry missed, but it can never rescue a part geometry already failed.
- When a mating part is **inserted, slid, or tilted into place**, check clearance
  along that path, not only at the final position: sweep the mating part through
  the travel in steps and measure overlap and minimum gap at each step, because a
  wall that clears the installed part can still block it on the way in.
- Re-check an earlier clearance after **every edit near it**: widening a gap on one
  side moves material toward something else, so rerun the clearance and path checks
  for the neighbours, not only for the feature you changed.
- Report only checks that actually ran. Never claim structural safety, tolerance
  compliance, or manufacturability unless that analysis was explicitly performed —
  geometric plausibility is the ceiling of what these checks prove.

## Worked Examples

Input: a copilot builds a 60×40×5 plate; spec says two Ø5.5 holes 40 mm apart.

Verification read:
1. Per feature (sketch, pad, hole): read each result only — `sketch_state`
   `fully_constrained` true and `dof` 0, `post_verify.passed` true,
   `tnp_audit.status` `CLEAN`, `changed` lists the new feature and the body. No
   `verify_*` call, no screenshot.
2. Milestone (plate finished). Baseline: `query_tree_summary` on the body
   (named, `*tip` last, no `!` line); `query_mass_properties` → bbox ≈ 60×40×5.
3. One `verify_shape` with every spec check in `checks`: `is_valid_solid`,
   `count_cylindrical_holes == 2`, `hole_diameter == 5.5`, `hole_spacing == 40`.
4. `query_screenshot` (single iso — simple static part per the packet guide). The
   holes look centered; nothing to escalate. Done: geometry ∧ visual both pass.

Input: a modification — "make the flange 5 mm taller" on a bracket built as
plate pad → hole pocket → flange pad → slot pocket.

Verification read: the `feature_set_parameters` result's `mutation.changed` lists
the flange pad, the slot pocket and the body — cumulative shapes, as expected —
and `fingerprint_before.digest` / `fingerprint_after.digest` differ. The plate pad and
the hole pocket are absent; if the hole pocket were listed, that is a silent
regression to investigate, not a success. The edit closes a milestone, so one
`verify_shape` re-measures the flange height, then one `query_screenshot`. A
clean recompute alone would have hidden the regression.

## Anti-Patterns

- **Recompute = done.** Symptom: a wrong part reported as passing. Why: the script
  ran, so it was assumed correct. Fix: follow every recompute with spec-driven
  measurement.
- **Skipping the render because the numbers passed.** Symptom: a mirrored or
  wrong-face part ships. Why: deterministic checks only encode what the spec
  listed; orientation and gestalt aren't in the numbers. Fix: screenshot every
  milestone; done is geometry ∧ visual.
- **Verifying every feature.** Symptom: a `verify_sketch`, `verify_shape` and
  screenshot after each step; a session spends most calls and context on checks.
  Why: the mutation result already reported `post_verify`, `sketch_state` and
  `changed`. Fix: read the result per feature; verify and render per milestone.
- **Claiming a visual finding as a result.** Symptom: "looks asymmetric" reported
  as a defect with no measurement. Why: a render is diagnostic, not authoritative.
  Fix: convert the concern into a `query_placement`/`query_mass_properties` check
  first.
- **File diff as geometry comparison.** Symptom: "the file changed, so the
  geometry changed" (or the reverse). Why: saved-document bytes shift for reasons
  unrelated to shape. Fix: compare the `mutation.fingerprint_*.digest` values and
  read `mutation.changed`.
- **Export written = export done.** Symptom: a STEP/STL delivered without a
  re-import check. Why: writing bytes isn't verifying geometry survived. Fix:
  require the paired `verify_export_*` before calling it done.
- **Treating `UNSUPPORTED` reference audit as clean.** Symptom: a silently
  corrupted model passes. Why: no-element-map was read as no-problem. Fix:
  `UNSUPPORTED` is not a pass.
- **Checking only the installed position.** Symptom: a part that "fits" cannot be
  assembled. Why: the interference check ran at the end pose only. Fix: sweep the
  assembly path and report overlap and minimum gap per step.
Plan: one body. Plate 60×40×5 centered on the origin, sketched on XY, padded 5 mm. A Ø10 circle at the center is then cut with a through-all pocket. I'll start with the document.
